# Deploy generated files

Deploys run from a local checkout; CI never deploys. Deploy only when the request asks for publication.

1. Run [Stage A](../verify.md#stage-a-pre-deploy). Stop if it fails.
2. Resolve the Git branch and the destination (an SSH host alias and the document root on it) from the request or secure local configuration. Never write resolved values into the repository.
3. Push the branch requested by the user. Do not substitute a different branch.
4. Derive the upload set: `.venv/bin/python scripts/site_diff.py <base> --visuals-base <visuals-base> > <rows>`, saving the rows to a file outside the repository for Stage B, where `<base>` is the commit whose build is live (the last deployed commit) and `<visuals-base>` the yujieteo/visuals commit that build read (`scripts/build.py` prints it), both resolved like the destination in step 2. Build from a clean yujieteo/visuals checkout at a commit on visuals main: a printed commit ending in `+dirty` read uncommitted changes, which no later deploy can rebuild, and `scripts/site_diff.py` refuses it as `--visuals-base`. A `<base>` that still pins its visualizations needs no `--visuals-base`. Record this deploy's commit and the visuals commit its build printed for the next deploy. `site/` is not committed, so the script rebuilds `<base>` and compares it file by file with the fresh `site/` from Stage A. It prints one `A` (added), `M` (modified) or `D` (no longer generated) row per file, `site/corpus.json` first. When unsure of `<base>`, choose an older commit: that only adds files whose bytes are already live.
5. Review that list. The upload set is every `A` and `M` path. It can include large pinned downloads, such as `site/visuals/beamdswitch/kokoro/**` (about 440 MB, the largest file 326 MB); they are listed only when their pin in `visuals/<slug>/raw.json` changed since `<base>`, or on their first deploy. Upload them like any other file, allowing for the transfer time, and install `visuals/beamdswitch/coi-serviceworker.js` in the same atomic install as `visuals/beamdswitch/index.html`, because the page does not load narration without it. Leave `D` paths on the host; never remove remote files. The changed files can include `notes.html`, `blog.html`, `papers.html`, `index.html`, `about.html`, `open-questions.html`, `colophon.html`, `visuals.html`, `blog/<slug>.html`, `media/**` (pages, audio, and video), `podcast/**` (legacy redirect pages and audio), and `visuals/**` (pages and `data.json`).
6. If public content changed, upload `site/corpus.json` first. Then upload every changed file under a unique temporary name, including non-HTML assets such as `site/media/audio/*.mp3`, `site/media/video/*.mp4`, `site/media/video/*.vtt`, `site/media/video/*.jpg`, and `site/visuals/*/data.json`. In a shell loop over the upload set, call `ssh -n` (or redirect its input from `/dev/null`) so `ssh` does not consume the list the loop is reading. If you bundle files with `tar`, run it as `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar ...`: macOS `tar` otherwise adds an AppleDouble `._*` file beside each file that carries extended attributes, and the server would serve them.
7. Follow [Atomic safe deploy](../principles/atomic-safe-deploy.md) for the complete upload set. Install every file with a web-readable mode (0644, or the mode the host documents) as part of the atomic install. Never rely on the upload tool's default mode: `scp` preserves a restrictive local mode, so a 0600 generated file stays unreadable to the web server.
8. Run [Stage B](../verify-post-deploy.md).

Principles: [No secrets in the repository](../principles/no-secrets-in-repo.md), [Atomic safe deploy](../principles/atomic-safe-deploy.md), and [Generated files are read-only](../principles/generated-files-are-read-only.md).
